subject: Social Media
title: Brain Development and Screens
description: A 60-second lesson on Brain Development and Screens.

hook.text: A 13-year-old's prefrontal cortex won't mature for another decade. That's the part that resists impulses.

buildup.text: Teen brains are uniquely vulnerable to social reward. Peer approval activates teen reward circuits far more than adults.

discovery.text: Social media delivers non-stop peer evaluation during the most sensitive developmental window.

twist.text: Adolescent brains show stronger responses to social media notifications than adult brains. They're wired to care more.

climax.text: The debate isn't whether teens are affected—they are. The debate is whether the damage is lasting.

punchline.text: The most vulnerable brains get the most exposure.

quiz.question: Why are teen brains more vulnerable to social media effects?
options: Their reward circuits respond more strongly to peer evaluation
